The post Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin , a design-and-review layer for AI coding agents. The Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin makes an agent write a specification before it writes code. Fresh subagents with no conversation history then attack that spec. Google says thousands of its engineers use it . It is quite simple: catch wrong assumptions in a Markdown file, not in a pull request. TL;DR Size: 7 skills, 9 reviewer personas, 6 brainstorm lenses, 5 review stages. No model weights; your agent supplies the LLM. Runs on: any harness that can spawn fresh subagents: Antigravity, Claude Code 2.1.271+, Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT. Uses your existing model quota. Performance: no accuracy benchmark published. Evidence is adoption and end-to-end harness test runs. Best: Codex 0.163.0 completed 15 native fresh-context reviewers in order. 2 live tests passed in 573.13s. Worst: the Claude Cowork run stopped after stages 5 to 7 on a usage limit. Issue #237 reports AGENTS.md leaking into Codex reviewers. Bottom line: best thing, forced independent review before code. Worst thing, heavy token use and unverified isolation on some hosts. What is Google’s Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin? EGM is an Apache 2.0 plugin of skills, reviewer personas and document standards. It is not a new language model. The method comes from Dave Rensin’s essay on elephants and goldfish. The Google Open Source blog frames it as a fix for AI “slop” and session context collapse. The README states it is not an officially supported Google product . How does the Elephant-Goldfish workflow work? The Elephant is a long session holding project context and earlier decisions. It drafts the spec and writes no code. Each Goldfish is a stateless subagent. It reads only the draft and the files it references. You resolve trade-offs and approve the design. The core loop has 3 commands: /egm-brainstorm clarifies the idea, then runs a 6-lens Goldfish swarm. Lenses cover YAGNI, token cost, UX, migration, observability and tech debt. Output: concepts_brief.md . /egm-draft turns the brief into a design doc under docs/designs/ , section by section. /egm-review runs the Goldfish review. /egm-drift-report later compares code with the spec. The docs recommend running it weekly. What happens in the 5-stage Goldfish review? The review skill runs 5 sequential stages: Initial Zoom Out: checks the whole document at a high level. Comprehension Test: a Goldfish paraphrases the design. A wrong paraphrase means the doc is ambiguous. Critic Review: design, structural and style reviewers hunt gaps and edge cases. Intermediate Zoom Out: rechecks architecture after fixes. Implementation Readiness: checks file paths, data structures and signatures. Each stage allows at most 1 re-audit. Findings are ranked Blocker, Major or Nit. If a host has no subagent tool, EGM stops. A same-context review is not a Goldfish review. Which coding agents does EGM support? Launch coverage described Antigravity-only support , with more coming. The current harness guide covers Antigravity CLI and App, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, Codex, ChatGPT, omp and Muse. Antigravity CLI, Claude Code and Codex pass automated end-to-end fixtures. Claude Code needs version 2.1.271 or later . Reviewers there get only Read, Grep and Glob tools. CLAUDE.md files are excluded from their context. The test record gives concrete run data: Antigravity CLI 1.4.5: 16 native reviewers ran, stages in order. Codex 0.163.0: 15 native reviewers, 2 live tests in 573.13s. Codex CLI with the v0.1.0 ZIP: full suite passed in 482.30s. How does EGM compare with Spec Kit, Kiro and Superpowers? Feature Google EGM GitHub Spec Kit Kiro Specs Superpowers Type Plugin (skills + personas) Toolkit + Specify CLI Feature of an agentic IDE/CLI/web Skills plugin License Apache 2.0 MIT Commercial ( pricing ) MIT Workflow Brainstorm, draft, review, drift report Constitution, specify, plan, tasks, implement, converge Requirements, design, tasks Brainstorm, plan, subagent build, TDD, review Spec reviewed by fresh-context subagents Yes, 5 stages before code Not disclosed Not disclosed (Analyze Requirements pass) No; fresh subagents review code per task Harness Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, more Copilot and other agents Kiro only 16 harnesses listed Setup Plugin install Python 3.11+, uv Kiro account Plugin install Cost Free plugin; host model usage Free toolkit; host model usage Subscription Free plugin; host model usage EGM’s distinct move is reviewing the spec with zero-context agents. Spec Kit and Kiro center on human review between phases. Superpowers isolates subagents mainly at implementation time. Key Takeaways EGM is a plugin, not a model: Elephant drafts, Goldfish reviews. Specs get 5 zero-context review stages before any code. Works across Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex and ChatGPT. Codex test runs completed 15 fresh-context reviewers end to end. Reviewer isolation still leaks host instruction files on some CLIs. Check out the GitHub repo , the project site and the Google Open Source blog post . DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral, Llama 4, gpt-oss Compared appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models share one idea but disagree on almost every routing detail. Expert counts range from 8 to 384. Top-k ranges from 1 to 8. Some models keep an always-on shared expert; others drop it. TL;DR Size: 10 models, from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (35B total, 3B active) to DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T total, 49B active). Runs on: gpt-oss-120b fits one 80 GB GPU with MXFP4; DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi K2 need multi-GPU expert parallelism. Performance: Routed sparsity spans 4x in Mixtral (8 experts, top-2) to 128x in Llama 4 Maverick (128, top-1). Best: Kimi K2 found sparsity 48 needed 1.69x fewer FLOPs than sparsity 8 at equal validation loss. Worst: Llama 4 Maverick and gpt-oss do not publish their gating or balancing method in config.json. Bottom line: Best thing: configs make routing fully auditable. Worst thing: names like “17B active” hide very different routers. How do open MoE models route tokens? Every model below uses token-choice routing: each token selects its own experts. They differ on 5 knobs. These are expert count, experts per token
